QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_32

question.text: What is the regulatory concentration limit for a Cat III AIF (open-ended) per SEBI, with respect to investment in a single investee company?

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III open-ended AIFs have a 10% single-investee concentration limit. Close-ended Cat III AIFs have a 25% limit. This is a SEBI prudential norm to control concentration risk. The Trap: 5% is too strict; 25% is the close-ended Cat III rule and the old Cat I/II norm; 35% is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D Cat I/II Manager tests 25% for close-ended; XIX-E tests the 10% open-ended Cat III rule. Manager's Pro-Tip: Monitor concentration DAILY — an illiquid holding can breach the 10% cap due to mark-up of a single name without any new purchase. Side-pocket or trim within T+2 to avoid breach.
